description: Nexus Platform — RED method. Gauge · Heatmap · Bar chart · State timeline. Select Instance to filter by node; adjust Rate Window when zooming into short time ranges.

panels.description: Non-5xx responses as % of all traffic. The arc fills green ≥ 99.9 %, turns yellow below 99 %, red below 98 %. Any red background = active incident.

panels.description: Server errors as % of traffic. Bar fills red as rate climbs. 0.1 % = warn; 1 % = page immediately.

panels.description: 99th-percentile request duration. Bar fills toward red as latency worsens. > 2 s = regression.

panels.description: Total HTTP requests per second across selected instances.
panels.title: Throughput

panels.description: Total BEAM heap across selected instances. > 1 GB on a single node warrants investigation.
panels.title: VM Memory

panels.description: Green = Prometheus scrape succeeded (node is up). Red = scrape failed (node is down or unreachable). Each row is one instance.
panels.title: Node Availability History

panels.description: Full histogram of request durations over time. Bright band = where most requests land. A wide diffuse band = high variance. A second faint band appearing at high latency = slow outliers. Y axis is log-scale milliseconds.
panels.title: HTTP Latency Distribution

panels.description: Server error rate over time. Dashed lines mark the 0.1 % warn and 1 % critical thresholds. Any time above the red line requires an incident response.

panels.title: 5xx Error Rate Trend

panels.description: HTTP throughput split by response class. 5xx (red) above zero = server errors in flight.
panels.title: Request Rate by Status Class

panels.description: Slowest endpoints ranked by P99. Green < 200 ms, yellow < 500 ms, orange < 1 s, red ≥ 1 s. Each bar is one route — the wider the bar the slower the endpoint.
panels.title: Top Endpoints — P99 Latency

panels.description: Total Ecto time (queue + execution + decode). Sustained P99 > 100 ms = slow queries or missing indexes. Compare with Queue Wait: if both spike together, it's pool saturation, not query slowness.
panels.title: Query Duration — P50 / P95 / P99

panels.description: Time queries spend waiting for a free connection. P95 > 10 ms = pool saturated. Raise pool_size in config or reduce query concurrency. Spikes at 2–3 AM = Oban cron jobs.
panels.title: DB Connection Pool — Queue Wait P50 / P95 / P99

panels.description: Configured Ecto connection pool size.
panels.title: DB Pool Size

panels.description: Mean DB execution time excluding pool queue and decode.
panels.title: Avg Query Execution

panels.description: Ecto query throughput across selected instances.
panels.title: Query Rate

panels.description: Rows returned per query. Rising P99 = unpaginated queries fetching unbounded result sets — correlate with Binary memory spikes.
panels.title: Results Returned — P50 / P95 / P99

panels.description: Time Ecto spends deserialising Postgres wire results into Elixir structs. High decode relative to execution = too many rows or large binary columns.
panels.title: Query Decode Time — P50 / P95 / P99

panels.description: BEAM allocator categories stacked. Processes + Binary dominate in a Phoenix app. Monotonically growing Binary = large binaries not being GC'd. Growing ETS = unbounded table.
panels.title: Memory Breakdown

panels.description: Number of tasks currently running on BEAM schedulers per node. Sustained count near your CPU core count = CPU-bound. Confirm with Run Queue Length.
panels.title: Active Scheduler Tasks

panels.description: BEAM processes and ports per node. Monotonically increasing process count = process leak. Check with :recon.proc_count(:message_queue_len, 10).
panels.title: Process & Port Count

panels.description: Processes waiting to be scheduled. Threshold lines shown on graph: yellow at 5, red at 20. Sustained high run queue = CPU bottleneck — identify hot processes with :recon_trace.
panels.title: Scheduler Run Queue Length

panels.description: Left axis: GC runs per second. Right axis: bytes freed per second. Spikes after traffic bursts are normal. Sustained high GC at low traffic = large long-lived process heaps.
panels.title: GC Collections & Bytes Reclaimed

panels.description: Context switches/s (left) = scheduler switching frequency. Reductions/s (right) = total CPU work. Rising reductions with flat switches = a few processes monopolising CPU.
panels.title: Context Switches & Reductions

panels.description: Time to complete mount/2 including any DB queries on mount. P99 > 500 ms = slow initial page load for 1 in 100 users. Shows data only when LiveView activity occurs in the selected time window. Empty panels indicate no user interactions during this period — this is correct behaviour.
panels.title: LiveView Mount Duration — P50 / P95 / P99

panels.description: Time to process handle_event/3. Sustained P99 > 200 ms = clicks feel sluggish. Check for synchronous DB calls inside event handlers. Shows data only when LiveView activity occurs in the selected time window. Empty panels indicate no user interactions during this period — this is correct behaviour.
panels.title: LiveView Handle Event Duration — P50 / P95 / P99

panels.description: Unhandled exceptions in mount/2 and handle_event/3. Any sustained non-zero rate = code crashing in production. Correlate with error logs below.
panels.title: LiveView Exception Rate

panels.description: Total socket connections established since last restart, split by transport. Longpoll reconnects on every page navigation; WebSocket holds a persistent connection. This app uses longpoll transport for LiveView.
panels.title: Socket Connects — Longpoll vs WebSocket (cumulative)

panels.description: Error and warning lines from all Nexus nodes. Use the shared crosshair to correlate log spikes with the panels above.
panels.title: Application Error Logs
